hero.lead: A nation of 19.7 million that cut its external debt from $5.3 billion to $0.6 billion in five years, and where more than half of citizens are undernourished.

capital.heading: 18 instruments. Debt relief completed, then budget support, safety nets, power, water and care.

record.text: Debt relief under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries Initiative: external public debt, end-2018 to end-2023
IMF Extended Credit Facility after the augmentation of December 2025, with about US$100 million disbursed
Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026, for 2.4 million people
BOOST-You: cash transfers and youth employment for about 738,000 people
Somali Electricity Sector Recovery Project, for about 7 million people

register.name: Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
register.detail: Launched 26 January 2026 · 2.4 million people targeted, 1.6 million prioritised in 21 high-risk districts
register.text: The appeal of the United Nations and humanitarian partners for lifesaving aid, essential services and protection in 2026. With limited resources, partners will put 1.6 million people in the most severe conditions first.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: Approved 19 December 2023 · fourth review completed and augmentation approved 8 December 2025 · total access SDR 105 million
register.note: About US$100 million disbursed after the fourth review
register.text: IMF budget support for the reforms that followed debt relief. The December 2025 augmentation added SDR 30 million (about US$40 million), and the fourth review released SDR 22.5 million (about US$30 million).

register.name: Building Opportunities and Outcomes in Social Protection and Youth Employment (BOOST-You)
register.detail: Approved, announced 28 October 2025 · $100 million IDA, $10 million Somalia Multi-Partner Fund, $2 million Global Shield Financing Facility
register.text: Regular and emergency cash transfers, cash transfers linked to health and education, and support for 28,000 jobs for young people by 2029, including 16,800 for women. It builds on the Baxnaano safety net and funds a national socio-economic survey.

register.name: Economic Resilience Development Policy Financing, second operation
register.detail: Approved, announced 7 August 2025 · IDA grant · the last of a series of two
register.note: Revenue, spending, renewable power, microfinance and fisheries
register.text: Budget support for reforms to raise domestic revenue, account for public spending, expand renewable power towards 50 MW of capacity by December 2026, develop microfinance and drought insurance, and grow seafood exports.

register.name: First Somalia Economic Resilience Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved, announced 30 July 2024 · IDA grant · the first of a series of two
register.note: Revenue, debt management and greener power
register.text: Budget support for stronger revenue collection, debt management and spending accountability, microfinance for lower-income groups including pastoralists, and greener, more affordable electricity.

register.name: Debt relief under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries Initiative
register.detail: Completion point approved 13 December 2023 by the IMF and IDA Boards
register.note: External public debt, end-2018 to end-2023
register.text: External public debt fell from US$5.3 billion, 64% of GDP, at end-2018 to US$0.6 billion, less than 6% of GDP, at end-2023. Debt relief reopened the door to concessional finance for the seven standards.

register.name: Shock Responsive Safety Net for Human Capital Project, third additional financing
register.text: Emergency cash transfers for households hit by floods and drought, and cash transfers linked to nutrition, for more than 250,000 Somali households.

register.name: Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation (ASCENT Somalia)
register.detail: Regional programme launched 28 November 2023, with Somalia among the first four countries · total project cost $100 million
register.note: Includes US$18.5 million from the Green Climate Fund
register.text: Increases access to sustainable and clean energy through private sector participation. Energy, measured by clean cooking, is the standard that sets Somalia’s Coverage.

register.name: Development Policy Financing on the path to debt relief, second operation
register.detail: Approved, announced 31 July 2023 · grant · the second of a series of two
register.note: Laws for fisheries, electricity, investment and data
register.text: Budget support for new laws on fisheries, electricity, investor protection, digital identification and data protection, for harmonised customs and a stronger external audit.

register.name: Barwaaqo: Somalia Water for Rural Resilience Project
register.text: Brings water to about 500,000 people in the drylands, roughly 15% of the rural population, who rely on unimproved or surface water. It builds on the Biyoole project, in Somaliland and five federal member states.

register.name: Somali Electricity Sector Recovery Project
register.note: About 7 million people in 1.1 million households
register.text: Rebuilds the electricity sector to reach about 7 million people, 3.5 million of them women, and to power 205 health facilities and 380 schools at lower cost.

register.name: Improving Healthcare Services in Somalia (Damal Caafimaad)
register.detail: Announced 22 July 2021 · $75 million IDA grant and $25 million GFF grant
register.note: Essential health services for about one in ten Somalis
register.text: Expands essential health and nutrition services in Nugaal, Bakool, Bay, Hiraan and Middle Shebelle, including for displaced and nomadic people. Health coverage stands at 30 on the WHO index.

register.name: Somalia Urban Resilience Project II
register.note: IDA $50 million and Somalia Multi-Partner Fund $62 million
register.text: Strengthens local government capacity and builds urban infrastructure in Somali cities.

register.name: Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Project in Dollow, Qardho and South Galkayo
register.detail: Approved 28 January 2026 · African Development Fund grant
register.note: More than half a million people
register.text: Safe water and sanitation for three fast-growing towns that have taken in many displaced people.

register.name: Rehabilitation and Expansion of Bosaso Power Grid
register.detail: Release of 16 December 2025 · grants: $9.618 million African Development Fund, $13.74 million Transition Support Facility
register.note: New solar generation and battery storage
register.text: Rebuilds and extends the Bosaso grid with solar power and battery storage, and gives solar home systems to families without electricity, including displaced people. It also trains energy sector institutions.

register.name: Activating Climate-Resilient Agricultural Livelihoods in Somalia
register.detail: Approved 2 December 2025 · African Development Fund grant
register.text: Climate-resilient farming and food security for 180,000 people directly and 300,000 more indirectly, including women, young people and pastoral households.

register.name: Strengthening Urban Resilience of Displaced and Host Communities in Doolow
register.detail: Release of 3 December 2025 · African Development Fund grant through the Transition Support Facility
register.text: Supports the local integration of more than 128,000 displaced people in Doolow, with secure land tenure for 10,500 and 1,750 climate-resilient homes. It also backs more than 150 village savings and loans associations.

register.name: IFC and KIMS Microfinance
register.detail: Approved 13 May 2026 · signed 2 July 2026 · three-year Sharia-compliant senior loan
register.note: Up to US$1 million, pending disbursement
register.text: A loan that KIMS Microfinance will on-lend to micro and very small enterprises in Somalia. It is backed by a pooled first-loss guarantee from IDA’s Private Sector Window.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Clean Ledger
items.label: External debt to GDP, end-2023, from 64%
items.text: Debt relief completed in December 2023 opens the door to new concessional finance.

items.name: The Coast
items.label: Natural resource rents, share of GDP, 2021
items.text: The longest coastline in mainland Africa, and its fisheries.
items.alt: The Somali coast on the Indian Ocean

items.name: The Herds
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Rangeland for camels, goats and sheep, the backbone of rural income.
items.alt: Camels and goats on the Somali rangeland

items.name: The Sun
items.label: Renewable share of electricity output, 2021
items.text: Strong sun and wind, and a grid still run mostly on diesel.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: More than half live in towns and cities.

items.name: BECO
items.text: Supplies electricity in Mogadishu and nearby towns, and is one of Somalia’s largest investors in solar power. Its tariff fell from $1.00 a kilowatt-hour in 2014 to $0.41 in 2023.

items.name: KIMS Microfinance
items.text: A Somali microfinance institution that lends to micro and very small enterprises. IFC has advised it since 2018 and signed a Sharia-compliant loan of up to US$1 million with it in July 2026.
